To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the density-dependent M3Y effective nucleon-nucleon interaction, with a strength of 25% below saturation, provides an excellent description of the elastic and inelastic scattering of 25- to 140-MeV α particles from 12C, 16O, 28Si, 40Ca, and 90Zr targets.
the folding model is a good description of the elastic scattering of α particles from 25 to120 MeV and of inelastic scattering from 25 to about 90 MeV.

the density dependence of the M3Y effective force is essential for the folding model to be applicable to the description of α-particle elastic and inelastic scattering, that the folding model can describe the elastic scattering at all energies, that it describes the inelastic scattering at energies below 100 MeV, but fails at higher energies, and that the neutron contributions to the transition multipole moments are generally smaller than the proton contributions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (a) the density dependence of the M3Y effective nucleon-nucleon interaction and its application to elastic α scattering, (b) the extension of the density-dependent model to inelastic α scattering and the determination of neutron transition densities, and (c) a comparison of the results of the present research to those from other research.
the following topics: 1) The density dependence of the semi-real effective M3Y force is examined.

the following: (i) the folding model with density-dependent M3Y interaction is applied to the study of elastic and in-elastic α-particle scatterings, and (ii) the neutron transition multipole moment is derived from (α, α’) data and compared with those derived from ( p, p’) data at 800 MeV, as well as from other sources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the folding model, with the density-dependent M3Y effective force, is an effective tool for the analysis of α-particle elastic and inelastic scattering, at least for the nuclei studied.

the folding model with the M3Y force is a useful tool for describing elastic α-particle scattering at intermediate and higher energies, and that it is also useful for describing inelastic scattering at intermediate energies.

the folding model is able to account for the data in a consistent way, and that it provides a reasonable description of the transition multipole moments, although the neutron transition moments obtained from (α, α’) data are systematically lower than those obtained from (p, p′) data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, with the exception of the 2 ^{+} state, the model is able to account for all the elastic scattering data, and the inelastic scattering data are also well described, including the relative strengths of the different transitions, with the exception that the model predicts a stronger 2 ^{+1} → 2 ^{+2} transition than observed.
a folding model with a realistic interaction and a realistic description of the transition densities can be used to analyze the elastic and inelastic data at energies from 25 MeV to 800 MeV.
the density-dependent folding model with M3Y provides a good description of elastic and inelastically scattered data, including both the collective and the polarization parts.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the density-dependent folding model can be used successfully to analyze both elastic and inelastic scattering data over a wide range of energies, and that the neutron transition densities can be constrained by the data.

a folding model with a semi-realistic effective interaction and density-dependent nucleon-nucleon potential can be used to analyze both elastic and inelastic (α, α’) scattering data over a large energy range, and that the resulting neutron transition densities are consistent with other sources.
a density-dependent folding model with the semi-realistic form of the M3Y interaction can describe elastic scattering data from 25 to ∼ 200 MeV.
